title: Distribution, Channel/MSP Partners, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
book_title: The Channel Flywheel and the Anatomy of a Dollar of Revenue

epigraph.quote: Direct sales forces scale linearly with headcount; multi-tenant channel platforms scale exponentially with partner margin.
epigraph.author: B2B Software Distribution Principle

web_blocks.html: Unlike enterprise peers that rely heavily on costly direct reps, AvePoint runs a hybrid channel-first go-to-market model. By FY2025, 57% of total ARR came through channel partners—MSPs, Value-Added Resellers (VARs), and Systems Integrators (SIs)—up from 55% in FY2024 [2, 7]. Direct enterprise sales made up the remaining 43% [2, 7]. Inside the channel, Managed Service Providers (MSPs) are the fastest-growing engine via AvePoint Elements. MSP-driven ARR jumped 55% from $40M in FY2024 to $62M in FY2025 [7, 9].

The unit-economic logic is clear. Selling a $15,000–$30,000 annual contract to a 250-seat law firm via a direct rep destroys margin once sales compensation and support are included. AvePoint Elements solves that math. Bolstered by the 2025 acquisition of Ydentic, Elements lets MSPs manage backup, governance, and identity across hundreds of SMB tenants from one console [9, 14]. AvePoint collects wholesale recurring software revenue at near-zero marginal sales cost. Meanwhile, the MSP builds a high-margin managed security practice on top. Multi-tenant automation also cuts partner support overhead, keeping MSP retention sticky even as AvePoint scales past $62M in MSP ARR [7, 9].

On the cost side, AvePoint's primary Cost of Revenue ($108.8M in FY2025, or 25.9% of sales) covers hyperscaler compute and object storage [1, 2]. That runs primarily on Microsoft Azure, alongside AWS and Google Cloud, plus bandwidth, support staff, and capitalized software amortization [1, 2]. Backup workloads store petabytes of snapshots across regional data centers to meet residency rules. Cloud storage and API transaction fees are therefore the key variable input to gross margin, which expanded to 74.1% GAAP in FY2025 [2].

The FY2025 operating expense lines show where leverage sits. Sales & Marketing (S&M) totaled $144.0M (34.3% of revenue), including $20M+ of amortized deferred sales commissions under ASC 606 [2, 6]. As channel partners absorb more mid-market acquisition, S&M has room to step down toward the high-20% range. Research & Development (R&D) was lean at $52.6M (12.5% of revenue), helped by global engineering hubs in Singapore and Asia alongside US teams [2, 13]. General & Administrative (G&A) stood at $81.1M (19.3% of revenue), elevated by stock-based compensation and dual-listing compliance (Nasdaq plus SGX) [2, 13]. Holding G&A dollar growth to single digits while revenue grows 20%+ would deliver 300 to 400 bps of GAAP margin expansion [2]. Upfront annual billing creates $201.0M of deferred revenue at year-end 2025, letting CFO ($85.3M) exceed GAAP operating income ($33.0M) by 2.58x [1, 2]. That customer float funds growth without external debt or equity dilution [1, 2].

Because AvePoint reports GAAP operating expenses by function (S&M $144.0M, R&D $52.6M, G&A $81.1M), employee payroll and SBC ($39.3M) are embedded within those functional lines rather than broken out separately on the P&L face.

web_blocks.mechanism: An MSP-centric backup and RMM leader (Datto) acquired in a leveraged buyout by Kaseya, followed by aggressive contract bundling, multi-year lock-in terms, billing friction, and support consolidation.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: After reporting $618.7M in FY2021 revenue and $658.4M in ARR, Datto was taken private by Kaseya in June 2022 for $6.2B ($35.50 per share in cash); subsequent contract restructuring and support consolidation triggered widespread MSP partner backlash and migration toward independent channel alternatives.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: AvePoint's 57% channel mix is a durable moat only as long as MSPs earn attractive services margins on AvePoint Elements; any aggressive price hikes or direct-sales channel conflict would immediately show up in GRR.

web_blocks.title: The Cloud Storage & API Cost Watchpoint
paragraphs: AvePoint's Resilience Suite stores massive volumes of customer backup data on hyperscaler infrastructure. Gross margin reached 74.1% in FY2025 thanks to SaaS mix and storage tiering in AvePoint Opus [1, 2]. Still, changes in Microsoft's M365 Backup Storage API pricing or cloud egress fees could pressure gross margins unless passed through in per-seat or per-GB tiers [1, 16]. Services revenue ($53.8M in FY2025, 12.8% of total revenue) also carries lower gross margins than SaaS. Keeping services as an onboarding bridge rather than a permanent drag is vital to holding 74%+ gross margins [1, 2]. Meanwhile, maintaining major R&D centers in Singapore alongside US teams keeps R&D at 12.5% of revenue ($52.6M in FY2025) while sustaining multi-cloud product velocity [2, 13]. Compared with physical storage peers like Backblaze (~62%–64% GAAP gross margin and heavy drive CapEx), AvePoint's software-layer model keeps CapEx at just 1.3% of revenue [2, 20]. As channel partners absorb more mid-market onboarding, S&M (34.3%) and G&A (19.3%) provide clear operating-margin runway [2, 7].

book_paragraphs: When you and I trace a dollar of revenue through AvePoint's income statement, the first surprise is not the 74.1% GAAP gross margin—that is table stakes for scaled SaaS. The real insight sits in how AvePoint acquires its customers without burning cash. In FY2025, 57% of AvePoint's ARR flowed through channel partners—Managed Service Providers, Value-Added Resellers, and Systems Integrators—up from 55% in FY2024. Even more telling, the Managed Service Provider slice of that channel jumped 55% year-over-year, from $40 million in FY2024 to $62 million in FY2025.

book_subsections.title: Why the MSP Channel Solves Mid-Market Unit Economics
paragraphs: Think about the math of selling enterprise software below the Fortune 1000. A direct enterprise Account Executive with a $250,000+ fully loaded compensation package simply cannot profitably chase $15,000 or $25,000 annual contracts at regional law firms, clinics, or municipalities. Customer acquisition cost would eat two years of gross profit. AvePoint solved that geometry problem by building AvePoint Elements, a multi-tenant control plane that lets an MSP manage backup, governance, and Microsoft 365 permissions across fifty or five hundred client tenants from a single screen.

To deepen that moat, AvePoint acquired Ydentic in early 2025, adding automated identity and access workflows directly into Elements. The MSP does the local selling, bundling, and first-line support, earning healthy services margins on top of AvePoint's software; AvePoint collects wholesale recurring SaaS revenue at near-zero marginal sales cost. That is also why the Datto-Kaseya cautionary tale matters: after Kaseya took Datto private for $6.2 billion in 2022, aggressive bundling and support friction alienated MSPs, reminding every channel vendor that partner trust is an asset you can lose in a single billing cycle.

book_subsections.title: Cloud Supply Chain and Global Engineering Arbitrage
paragraphs: Because AvePoint is a SaaS platform, it has no factories or physical inventory, yet it does have a very real digital supply chain: hyperscaler cloud compute and object storage on Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. In FY2025, Cost of Revenue was $108.8 million, or 25.9% of revenue, reflecting petabytes of encrypted customer backups stored across regional data centers to satisfy FedRAMP, GDPR, and local data-residency rules. As SaaS grew to 76.1% of revenue and storage-tiering tools like AvePoint Opus improved data efficiency, GAAP gross margin expanded to 74.1%.

Below the gross profit line, look at the three operating expense buckets. Sales & Marketing consumed $144.0 million (34.3% of revenue), including more than $20 million of amortized sales commissions. Research & Development was remarkably lean at $52.6 million (12.5% of revenue), helped by AvePoint's large engineering presence in Singapore and Asia alongside US teams. General & Administrative was $81.1 million (19.3% of revenue)—higher than ideal due to stock-based compensation and dual-listing compliance, which gives management a clear cost-leverage target as revenue scales.

book_subsections.title: Walking the FY2025 $419.5 Million Revenue-to-Cash Waterfall
paragraphs: Put the whole FY2025 waterfall together and you see why AvePoint's cash engine is stronger than its GAAP income statement looks. Start with $419.5 million of revenue. Subtract $108.8 million in cost of revenue to get $310.7 million of gross profit. Subtract $277.7 million in total GAAP operating expenses—which already absorb $39.3 million of non-cash stock-based compensation and $6.2 million of depreciation and amortization—and you land at $33.0 million in GAAP operating income. Add $7.5 million of net interest and other income, subtract $5.4 million in taxes, and GAAP net income finishes at $35.1 million. Finally, because customers pay annual subscriptions upfront—building a $201.0 million deferred revenue balance—operating cash flow surged to $85.3 million. After just $5.3 million in property, equipment, and capitalized software expenditures, Free Cash Flow reached $80.0 million, a 19.1% margin and 228% conversion of GAAP net income.

Now let us stress-test the unit economics underneath that waterfall for potential cracks. First, examine Sales & Marketing at $144.0 million, or 34.3% of revenue. Because ASC 606 requires software companies to capitalize and amortize sales commissions over the expected customer life, more than $20 million of that S&M line represents non-cash amortization of prior-year commissions. As channel partners and MSPs drive a larger share of new bookings—already 57% of ARR—direct commission intensity per dollar of net new ARR should continue trending down.

Second, examine the cloud storage margin risk. Unlike pure workflow SaaS tools that store tiny text databases, AvePoint's Resilience Suite stores petabytes of customer backups on hyperscaler object storage. That makes Azure and AWS storage pricing, API call fees, and data-egress charges a permanent variable cost. AvePoint mitigates this through intelligent data lifecycle tiering in AvePoint Opus—moving stale, redundant files out of expensive hot storage—which helped lift GAAP gross margin from 71.5% in FY2023 to 74.1% in FY2025. Still, if Microsoft ever alters wholesale M365 Backup Storage API pricing, AvePoint will need to pass those costs through cleanly in its per-seat and capacity tiers to defend its 74%+ gross margin.

Third, think about what the 57% channel mix implies for long-term operating leverage. In a pure direct-sales enterprise model, growing ARR from $500 million to $1 billion requires hiring hundreds of quota-carrying Account Executives and Solutions Engineers, which keeps Sales & Marketing stubbornly pinned at 35% to 40% of revenue. By contrast, when an MSP standardizes its Microsoft 365 practice on AvePoint Elements, every new small-business client that MSP signs flows onto AvePoint's platform with near-zero incremental sales cost. That is why MSP ARR jumped 55% in FY2025 to $62 million—and why AvePoint's S&M ratio has a credible path downward even as top-line ARR compounds above 20%.

Fourth, look at the role of professional services inside unit economics. Some pure-play software investors dislike seeing $53.8 million of Services revenue—12.8% of FY2025 sales—because services carry lower gross margins than recurring SaaS. At AvePoint, however, services act as a migration wedge: complex enterprise consolidations and government archive projects require engineering hand-holding upfront, which then locks the customer into multi-year Resilience and Control subscriptions. As long as Services stay in the 10% to 13% range and SaaS continues expanding past 80% of total revenue, the consolidated gross margin trajectory remains upward.

Fifth, do not overlook the cash-conversion mechanics of annual upfront billing. When AvePoint closes a three-year enterprise contract or an annual channel renewal, cash arrives upfront into deferred revenue ($201.0 million at year-end 2025) while revenue trickles onto the income statement month by month. That negative working-capital cycle means AvePoint effectively finances its own growth using customer float rather than external debt or dilutive equity.

Sixth, compare AvePoint's unit economics against pure storage-infrastructure peers like Backblaze. A commodity storage provider spends heavily on physical hard drives, data-center racks, and colocation power, resulting in ~62%–64% GAAP gross margins and persistent CapEx intensity. AvePoint sits one layer higher in the software stack: by running on elastic hyperscaler cloud storage while charging per-seat for automated backup, governance, and AI readiness, AvePoint captures a 74.1% GAAP gross margin while keeping total CapEx at just 1.3% of revenue ($5.3 million out of $419.5 million). That asset-light architecture is what turns 7.9% GAAP operating margin into a 19.1% Free Cash Flow margin.

Seventh, watch how G&A expense behaves as a percentage of revenue over the next two years. At $81.1 million, or 19.3% of FY2025 revenue, G&A is heavier than best-in-class enterprise SaaS peers, reflecting stock-based compensation and dual-listing compliance across Nasdaq and SGX. Holding G&A dollar growth to single digits while revenue grows 20%+ would deliver 300 to 400 basis points of GAAP operating margin expansion on top of Sales & Marketing leverage.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The beauty of upfront annual SaaS billing paired with a 57% channel engine is a 19% Free Cash Flow margin on a business still growing revenue 27%. The fragility to watch is G&A at 19.3% of revenue and S&M at 34.3%—and whether Microsoft's underlying storage API fees ever squeeze that 74.1% gross margin.
